originalPrompt: portable weather station with a display and 3 buttons
projectDescription: Portable Weather Station built around a ESP32-C3 SuperMini with BME280 Temp/Humidity/Pressure, 12 mm Tactile Push Button, 2.9in e-Paper 296x128 (SPI); battery-powered (≈10.4 h per charge), housed in a PETG enclosure.
plan:
- Main Controller: ESP32-C3 SuperMini — $2.90/unit; lowest price among candidates
- BME280 Temp/Humidity/Pressure: BME280 Temp/Humidity/Pressure — $3.20/unit; very common part (libraries & tutorials)
- Button 1: 12 mm Tactile Push Button — $0.05/unit; lowest price among candidates
- Button 2: 12 mm Tactile Push Button — $0.05/unit; lowest price among candidates
- Button 3: 12 mm Tactile Push Button — $0.05/unit; lowest price among candidates
- Display: 2.9in e-Paper 296x128 (SPI) — $13.00/unit; named in the prompt: display
- Battery: LiPo 3.7 V 1000 mAh (503450, PCM) — $3.50/unit; matches rechargeable
- USB-C Charger + Protection: TP4056 USB-C Li-ion Charger + Protection — 1S Li-ion needs CC/CV charging and over-discharge protection
- 5V Boost: MT3608 Boost Converter (set 5 V) — $0.50/unit; lowest price among candidates
- Power: li-po 3.7 Wh, est. runtime 10.4 h
- Enclosure: 110×75×25 mm in PETG

nodes.name: Main Controller
nodes.description: Tiny RISC-V 160 MHz board with Wi-Fi + BLE 5, USB-C. Few GPIO; great for small sensors.
rationale: rejected: esp32-cam (ESP32-CAM (AI-Thinker) + OV2640 has no SPI bus)

nodes.name: Battery
rationale: 3.7 Wh vs 1.7 Wh needed for 4 h

nodes.name: USB-C Charger + Protection
rationale: 1S Li-ion needs CC/CV charging and over-discharge protection

nodes.name: 5V Boost
rationale: boost: 3–4.2 V → 5 V, 1000 mA ≥ peak 350 mA

nodes.name: Enclosure Base
nodes.description: Printed tray 110×75×25 mm, 2 mm walls, integrated M2.5 bosses.

nodes.name: Enclosure Lid
nodes.description: Lid with 1 display window(s); screws into base bosses.

nodes.name: M2.5 Brass Standoffs
rationale: lift boards 5 mm off the floor for wiring clearance

assumptions: Slicer (PrusaSlicer/Cura/Bambu Studio) configured for the listed materials
PlatformIO (VS Code extension or CLI) installed
Lithium battery safety: never short, puncture or charge unattended

subSteps.title: Test-fit boards on standoffs before wiring
Assemble the power path (battery, charger, regulators)
Solder I2C bus lines to BME280 Temp/Humidity/Pressure
Solder SPI bus lines to Display
Verify continuity and rail voltages before inserting the MCU
Mount boards and modules inside the enclosure
Install panel parts (display/controls) into the lid
Close the enclosure and fasten the lid
